newsitem.title: USA: ITT confirms interest in Ciga.
newsitem.headline: ITT confirms interest in Ciga.

text.p: ITT Corp Wednesday confirmed reports it is considering several expressions of interest from parties interested in buying a portion of its 70- percent equity interest in Ciga Hotels Spa and individual Ciga hotels.
"ITT is considering all of its options regarding its position in Ciga, as well as other hotels, taking into account the best interests of its shareholders," the company said in a release.
ITT spokesman James Gallagher said that Ciga has about 30 hotels, but declined to say which individual hotels are being considered.
He also declined to identify the interested parties.
ITT bought the stake in Ciga, an Italy-based group of European luxury hotels, in 1994 as part of a geographical expansion. Public shareholders own the rest of the company.
Shares of Ciga had risen recently on speculation that ITT might be willing to sell its stake.
Gallagher said potential suitors have expressed interest in the entire stake, as well as portions of it.
"All we are saying is that we have been approached. We are examining the expressions of interest," he said.

The Ciga properties are the latest assets under consideration for sale by ITT, which is fighting a $6.5 billion hostile takeover from Hilton Hotels Corp. ITT also has received buying interest on its luxury St. Regis hotel in New York and Phoenician hotel in Arizona.
The hotel and casino giant also is in talks to sell its Desert Inn and Tunica casino properties.

ITT has sold several holdings since Hilton launched the bid in January, including its stake in Madison Square Garden. The company has said it will consider selling non-core assets in an attempt to focus on its Sheraton and Caesars World businesses.
A spokesman for Hilton Hotels rejected ITT's contention that it is considering the best interest of shareholders.
"If they were genuinely considering the best interest of their shareholders, what they'd be doing is talking to us," said spokesman Marc Grossman.
